title: Robustness & security idioms
literature: Secure design patterns (Schumacher POSA-security); OWASP; Viega & McGraw Building Secure Software; Saltzer & Schroeder principles; sandboxing/isolation idioms.

members.name: Access Control List
members.what: Store, with each protected object, the list of subjects and the operations each may perform on it; checks consult the object's list.

members.name: Allowlist Input Validation
members.what: Validate untrusted input by accepting only what matches an explicit specification of the known-good (type, length, range, grammar) and rejecting everything else.

members.name: Audit Log
members.what: An append-only record of security-relevant events (who did what, when, from where), written at the point of action for later reconstruction and accountability.

members.name: Authenticated Encryption
members.what: Encrypt and authenticate a message in one construction (optionally binding unencrypted associated data), so ciphertext cannot be undetectably modified.

members.name: Canonicalization Before Validation
members.what: Reduce input (paths, URLs, Unicode strings) to its single canonical form before applying validation or access checks, so equivalent encodings cannot slip past the check.

members.name: Capability
members.what: An unforgeable token/reference that both designates an object and carries the authority to use it; possession is permission (the row-slice of the access matrix).

members.name: Check Point
members.what: A single configurable object/component that concentrates authentication, authorization and violation-response decisions, so the security policy can change without touching callers.

members.name: Constant-Time Comparison
members.what: Compare secret-dependent data (MACs, tokens, passwords hashes) with an algorithm whose running time and memory access pattern are independent of the data values.

members.name: Cryptographic Hash Function
members.what: A fixed-size digest function that is one-way and collision-resistant, used for integrity fingerprints, content addressing, commitment, and as a building block for MACs and signatures.

members.name: Cryptographically Secure Pseudorandom Number Generator
members.what: A random generator whose output is computationally unpredictable even to an observer of prior output, seeded from real entropy, for keys, tokens, nonces and salts.

members.name: Defensive Copy
members.what: Copy mutable inputs on receipt and mutable internal state on return, so external aliases can never mutate an object's invariant-protected state.

members.name: Dual Channel
members.what: Two parallel channels (identical or diversely implemented) process the same inputs, with comparison or switchover logic detecting faults and continuing or safing on disagreement.

members.name: Full View With Errors
members.what: Show users the complete set of operations/data and reject unauthorized attempts with explicit errors at use time.

members.name: Guard Page
members.what: Place an inaccessible (or trap-on-touch) memory page or poisoned band adjacent to a stack or allocation so that overrun/overflow faults immediately at the boundary instead of corrupting neighbors.

members.name: HTML Sanitization
members.what: Parse untrusted markup into a DOM and rebuild it keeping only an allowlist of safe elements/attributes, yielding markup that renders but cannot execute script.

members.name: Limited View
members.what: Present users only the operations and data their permissions allow, so unauthorized actions cannot even be attempted.

members.name: Memory Poisoning
members.what: Fills freed or uninitialized memory with a recognizable poison pattern and verifies it later (on reallocation or access), so stale reads, use-after-free, and buffer overruns surface as the pattern or its corruption.

members.name: Message Authentication Code
members.what: A keyed digest over a message that only holders of the secret key can produce or verify, authenticating both integrity and origin.

members.name: Nonce
members.what: A value used exactly once within a security context (random, counter, or timestamp-based) so that replayed or duplicated messages/operations are detectable and rejected.

members.name: One's Complement Data Storage
members.what: Critical data is stored twice - once normally, once bit-inverted - and every read verifies the pair still complement each other before use.

members.name: Parameterized Query
members.what: Send the query text and the data values to the interpreter separately, so values are bound as data and can never be parsed as code.

members.name: Pointer Check
members.what: Explicitly set pointers to an invalid value (NULL) when uninitialized or freed, and check pointers against that invalid value before dereferencing them.

members.name: Privilege Bracketing
members.what: Hold elevated privilege only across the exact operations that need it: raise at the last possible moment, perform the action, drop immediately after (and permanently once never needed again).

members.name: Privilege Separation
members.what: Split one application into a small privileged process and unprivileged worker processes that request sensitive operations over a narrow IPC interface, so a compromise of the exposed code yields no privileges.

members.name: Program Sequence Monitoring
members.what: Instrument checkpoints along required execution paths and have a monitor (often the watchdog manager) verify that checkpoints occur in the legal order and cadence.

members.name: Protected Single Channel
members.what: A single end-to-end data/processing channel augmented with integrity checks at one or more points (CRCs, range checks, monitoring) so faults are detected even without redundant channels.

members.name: Reference Monitor
aka: policy enforcement point / policy decision point (operational split)
members.what: A component that mediates every access by subjects to protected objects, checking each request against the authorization rules before allowing it.

members.name: Role-Based Access Control
members.what: Authorization is granted to named roles rather than individual users; users acquire permissions by role membership, with optional role hierarchies.

members.name: Salted Password Hashing
members.what: Store passwords only as the output of a deliberately slow one-way function over password plus per-entry random salt, so verification is possible but recovery and precomputation are not.

members.name: Sanity Check
members.what: A lightweight independent monitor verifies that outputs or system state remain within physically/logically plausible bounds, triggering fault handling when they do not.

members.name: Secure Access Layer
members.what: An application-internal layer that wraps the security mechanisms of the platforms it sits on (OS, database, network APIs), giving the application one coherent security interface.

members.name: Secure Boot Image Verification
members.what: Before transferring control, the bootloader cryptographically verifies the next stage or application image against a trusted public key, refusing or falling back on failure.

members.name: Secure Zeroization
members.what: Erase sensitive data (keys, passwords) from memory using an operation the compiler cannot optimize away, immediately after last use.

members.name: Security Session
members.what: An object holding an authenticated subject's identity and security attributes across a sequence of actions, so each request need not re-authenticate or re-derive permissions.

members.name: Single Access Point
aka: one entry point for security checks
members.what: Route all entry into a program or module through one guarded entry point where identity and validity checks run before anything else executes.

members.name: Smart Data
members.what: Data types that carry their own validity metadata (ranges, units, CRC) and check every set/get operation, rejecting or flagging out-of-range values.

members.name: Stack Canary
members.what: Place a secret guard value between a stack frame's buffers and its control data (return address); verify it before returning, aborting if a buffer overflow overwrote it.

members.name: Synchronizer Token Pattern
members.what: Embed a per-session (or per-request) unpredictable token in each legitimate form/request and verify it server-side, so cross-site forged requests lacking the token are rejected.

members.name: Taint Checking
members.what: Mark data from untrusted sources as tainted, propagate the mark through computations, and refuse (or flag) its use in sensitive sinks until it passes an explicit untainting step.

members.name: Watchdog
members.what: A hardware or software timer that must be periodically serviced ('kicked') by correctly running software; missing the deadline triggers reset or a safety action.
